_comment: Test vectors for the prose-narrative predicate (ADR-254 dose lane).
INTENT: ONE copy, read by BOTH the Go original proseNarrative() in
services/chora-consumption/internal/adapter/http/companion_handlers.go and the
Python port used by the kennel dose lane to decide OK vs FAILED.
STATUS 2026-08-23: CLOSED. The Go side now reads this file.
TestProseNarrative_SharedVectors in
services/chora-consumption/internal/adapter/http/companion_handlers_narrative_test.go
loads and iterates every vector below, so adding a vector here turns RED on
whichever implementation does not handle it. The control is real rather than
believed. Verified by four discriminating checks, not by a green run: a vector
Go must fail DOES fail; removing a required bare-scalar vector fails by name;
an empty vector list fails on an explicit vacuous-pass guard; and a missing
file fails loud AT the monorepo root rather than climbing out of a git
worktree into whatever checkout contains it.
The extras here (bare scalars, quoted string, fence-tag rules, NaN/Infinity)
pin semantics the Go ORIGINAL had no test for, and the original is what
renders to a learner. The bare-scalar four are required BY NAME by the Go
test: they pin the live Go-versus-TypeScript disagreement (DEBT-REGISTER 1.1,
Go rejects them via json.Valid, the FE asProse does not), so removing them
would silently un-pin the thing this file exists to pin.
DO NOT inline these cases into any implementation's test. An inline copy is
precisely the drift this file prevents.
_semantics: input -> expected output. Empty output means NOT PROSE (rejected).
Order of operations in the original: trim, unwrap one markdown fence, then
reject empty / leading brace / leading bracket / anything json.Valid accepts.
The fence unwrap is NOT optional: a fenced JSON body must reject, and fenced
prose must survive. A port that skips it accepts fenced JSON at a learner.
